title: Potato gnocchi with butter and sage
intro: Potatoes, flour and nothing else: soft and light, with brown butter and sage.

steps.t: Boil the potatoes whole in their skins, starting in cold water, until a fork slides in easily.
steps.label: Potatoes

steam.t: Steam the whole potatoes for about 30 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.

steps.t: Peel them while still hot and push them straight through a ricer onto the worktop.
Spread them out and let them cool slightly so the steam escapes.
steps.label: Steam

steps.t: Add flour and salt and knead quickly, just until the dough is soft and no longer sticky.
Roll into 2 cm ropes, cut into 2 cm pieces and roll them over the tines of a fork.
Lay the gnocchi on a floured tray without overlapping.
Melt the butter with the sage in a wide pan over low heat until just nutty brown.
Cook the gnocchi in batches in salted water and lift them out a minute after they float.
steps.label: Gnocchi

steps.t: Transfer them to the pan with a slotted spoon, toss gently and serve with Parmigiano.

tips.t: Use old floury potatoes and as little flour as possible: more flour means tougher gnocchi.
Freeze them raw, spaced out on a tray, then bag them; cook straight from frozen.
Bake them with tomato sauce and mozzarella and they become gnocchi alla sorrentina.

title: Gnocchi alla sorrentina
intro: Gnocchi in tomato sauce with stretchy mozzarella, baked until bubbling.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220 °C, with the grill if you have one; dice the mozzarella and let it drain.
Warm the tomato sauce in a wide pan with a few basil leaves.
Cook the gnocchi in salted water and drain them as soon as they float (shop-bought: follow the packet).
steps.label: Gnocchi

steps.t: Fold them into the sauce with half the mozzarella and half the Parmigiano.
Tip into a baking dish and top with the remaining mozzarella, Parmigiano and basil.
Bake until the mozzarella is melted and golden on top.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Let it rest for a couple of minutes and serve in small dishes or straight from the tray.

tips.t: Drain the mozzarella in a sieve for half an hour so it won't water down the sauce.
Smoked provola instead of mozzarella gives a bolder flavour.

title: Tagliatelle with porcini mushrooms
intro: Egg tagliatelle and porcini sautéed with garlic and parsley: a taste of the woods.

ing.n: fresh egg pasta dough (or fresh tagliatelle)

steps.t: Clean the porcini with a damp cloth and a small knife, without washing, and cut them into 5 mm slices.
Roll the dough thin (1 mm) and cut it into 7–8 mm ribbons; with ready-made fresh tagliatelle, skip this step.
Heat oil and butter with the crushed garlic, add the porcini and sauté over high heat until golden.
steps.label: Porcini

steps.t: Salt them, remove the garlic and add the parsley.
Cook the tagliatelle in salted water for 2–3 minutes (shop-bought: follow the packet).
steps.label: Tagliatelle

steps.t: Drain them into the pan with a ladle of pasta water and toss until the sauce turns creamy.
Serve with Parmigiano and a grind of pepper.

tips.t: Out of season, use 30 g soaked dried porcini plus 300 g button mushrooms and some soaking water.
Don't crowd the pan: the porcini should brown, not stew in their own juices.

title: Lasagne alla bolognese
intro: Egg pasta, ragù and béchamel in many thin layers: an Emilian Sunday.

ing.n: fresh egg pasta dough (or fresh lasagne sheets)

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Roll the dough thin and cut sheets to fit your dish (or use ready fresh sheets).
Blanch the sheets a few at a time in salted water and lay them on a tea towel; for ready sheets, follow the packet.
steps.label: Sheets

steps.t: Warm the ragù; if it's very thick, loosen it with a few spoonfuls of hot water.
Butter a dish of about 30×20 cm and spread a thin layer of béchamel and ragù on the bottom.
Alternate layers of pasta, ragù, béchamel and Parmigiano, up to 5–6 layers.
Finish with béchamel, ragù, plenty of Parmigiano and flakes of butter.
Bake until golden on top and bubbling at the edges.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Let it rest before cutting so the layers set.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Assemble it the day before and bake it the next day: the layers meld and it cuts more cleanly.
It freezes well in portions: reheat covered with foil at 180 °C for about 30 minutes.

title: Spinach and ricotta ravioli
intro: Thin egg pasta, creamy ricotta and spinach filling, nutty sage butter.

ing.n: fresh egg pasta dough (or fresh pasta sheets)

steps.t: Wilt the spinach in a pan with a pinch of salt.
steps.label: Spinach

steps.t: Squeeze it well, chop it and mix with ricotta, two thirds of the Parmigiano, yolk, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough into very thin sheets (1 mm); ready-made fresh sheets from the chiller are fine too.
Place a teaspoon of filling every 5 cm on half the sheet and brush water around each one.
Fold the other half over, press around the filling to push out air and cut with a pasta wheel.
Cook in gently boiling salted water until they float and the pasta is tender.
steps.label: Ravioli

steps.t: Meanwhile, melt the butter with the sage over low heat until it turns nutty brown.
Lift the ravioli into the butter, add a splash of pasta water and serve with Parmigiano.

tips.t: Squeeze the spinach until bone dry: a wet filling makes ravioli burst as they cook.
Freeze raw ravioli on a floured tray, then bag them; cook from frozen.

title: Orecchiette with turnip tops
intro: Hand-made orecchiette, bitter turnip tops and anchovies: Puglia in winter.

steps.t: Knead semolina, warm water and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes until smooth and firm; cover and rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile, trim the turnip tops: keep the florets, tender leaves and peeled stems.
Cut off a piece of dough, roll it into a 1 cm rope and cut it into 1 cm pieces.
Drag each piece across the board with a knife blade, then turn it inside out over your thumb into a little ear.
Toast the breadcrumbs in a pan with 1 tbsp oil until golden.
Cook the turnip tops and orecchiette together in plenty of salted water.
steps.label: Orecchiette

steps.t: Meanwhile, melt the anchovies in the oil with garlic and chili in a wide pan over low heat.
Drain everything, toss in the pan for a minute and serve with the toasted crumbs.

tips.t: With 350 g dried orecchiette you skip the dough: cook them with the greens for the packet time.
Only semolina and warm water, no egg: the dough stays elastic and the orecchiette rough.

title: Pici all’aglione
intro: Hand-rolled Tuscan noodles with a mellow sauce of stewed garlic and tomato.

steps.t: Knead flours, water, 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt until smooth; cover and rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile, slice the garlic and stew it in the remaining oil over very low heat without colouring.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes and chili, salt, and simmer until thick and the garlic falls apart.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Meanwhile, roll the dough 1 cm thick, cut into strips and roll them under your palms into 3–4 mm noodles.
Spread the pici on a tray dusted with semolina so they don't stick.
Cook in salted water until al dente but tender.
steps.label: Pici

steps.t: Drain into the sauce and toss for a minute with a ladle of pasta water.

tips.t: Stew the garlic slowly, almost confit: it turns sweet and creamy, never bitter.
Instead of the sauce, toss them with crumbs toasted in garlic oil for pici alle briciole.

title: Käsespätzle
intro: Swabian egg noodles layered with melted cheese and crispy butter-fried onions.

steps.t: Beat flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg with a wooden spoon until the batter bubbles and drops slowly.
Leave it to rest, covered.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile, slice the onions thinly and fry them in half the butter over medium heat until golden and crisp.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C and press the batter through a spätzle maker into boiling salted water, in batches.
When the spätzle float, lift them out with a slotted spoon.
steps.label: Spätzle

steps.t: In a buttered dish, layer the hot spätzle with grated cheese.
Top with the onions and put in the oven until the cheese has melted.
steps.label: Oven

tips.t: Serve with a green salad or a vinegary potato salad, as they do in Swabia.
No spätzle maker? Spread the batter on a wet board and scrape thin strips into the water with a knife.

title: Pierogi ruskie
intro: Polish dumplings filled with potato, fresh cheese and onion, served with sour cream.

steps.t: Boil the peeled, chopped potatoes in salted water until tender.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Meanwhile, knead flour, warm water, oil and a pinch of salt until smooth and elastic; cover and rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Chop the onions and fry them in the butter over medium heat until golden.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Mash the drained potatoes with the crumbled cheese, half the onions, salt and lots of pepper.
Roll the dough to 2 mm and cut 7–8 cm rounds with a glass.
Put a teaspoon of cooled filling in the centre, fold into a half-moon and pinch the edges to seal.
Cook a few at a time in gently boiling salted water; lift out 2 minutes after they float.
steps.label: Pierogi

steps.t: Serve with the remaining onions, their butter and sour cream.

tips.t: Next day, fry them in butter until golden and crisp.
As in Polish homes, add crisp bacon bits to the onions (no longer vegetarian).

title: Pizzoccheri from Valtellina
intro: Buckwheat ribbons, cabbage, potato, melted Casera cheese and sage butter.

steps.t: Knead both flours with the warm water for 5 minutes until compact; cover and rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile, dice the potatoes, shred the cabbage and thinly slice the Casera.
Roll the dough to 2–3 mm and cut it into 1×7 cm strips (or use dried pizzoccheri).
Drop potatoes and cabbage into plenty of boiling salted water.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Add the pizzoccheri and cook everything together (dried: follow the packet).
steps.label: Pizzoccheri

steps.t: Meanwhile, gently colour the crushed garlic and sage in the butter over low heat.
Lift everything out with a slotted spoon and layer it in a hot dish with Casera, Grana and pepper.
Pour over the sizzling butter, remove the garlic, mix gently and serve at once.

tips.t: Slice the Casera thinly and lay it on the boiling-hot pasta: it should melt, not cook.
In summer, swap the cabbage for chard or green beans, as they do in Valtellina.
